scholarships.title: Canada Postdoctoral Research Award (CPRA)
scholarships.official_source: Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC)

existing.description: The Canada Postdoctoral Research Award program recognizes and empowers the next generation of highly qualified innovators, knowledge workers and creative thinkers. It supports outstanding postdoctoral researchers in developing their research skills and provides the funding and flexibility needed to support their contributions to building world-class research capacity and to Canada's prosperity and competitiveness. For the September 2026 competition SSHRC publishes a value and duration of $70,000 per year for 2 years, with an application deadline of September 10, 2026 at 8:00 p.m. eastern.
eligibility: Be a postdoctoral researcher seeking to develop research skills in Canada

Submit the four components required by SSHRC: the applicant application, a referee's Letter of Appraisal, the proposed supervisor's Research Appraisal, and the Institutional Nomination and Commitment form
existing.eligibility_summary: The programme supports outstanding postdoctoral researchers in developing their research skills. Applicants apply through SSHRC, one of the three federal research agencies, and the SSHRC page links separate instructions for the applicant, for referees using the Letter of Appraisal form, for the proposed supervisor using the Research Appraisal form, and for the Institutional Nomination and Commitment form.
benefits: Funding and flexibility to support the awardee's contribution to building world-class research capacity and to Canada's prosperity and competitiveness

Eligibility for separately competed supplements and joint initiatives, including the Alice Wilson Award, the Bora Laskin National Fellowship in Human Rights Research, the CHCI-SSHRC Postdoctoral Fellowships Collaboration, the Department of National Defence MINDS Scholarship Initiative, the Indigenous Scholars Awards and Supplements Pilot Initiative, the Jules and Gabrielle Leger Fellowship, Mitacs Training, and the Sport Participation Research Initiative
coverage: Canada Postdoctoral Research Award value of $70,000 per year for 2 years
requirements: Apply to the agency aligned with research subject (CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC)
Research proposal significantly distinct from doctoral thesis
documents: The referee has accepted the invitation. Referees who have accepted will be able to view an electronic version of your application to inform their letter of reference.
application_method: Submit the applicant application per the SSHRC 2026 Applicant instructions
Arrange for a referee to submit a Letter of Appraisal using the SSHRC form
Have the proposed supervisor complete the Research Appraisal form
Have the institution complete the Institutional Nomination and Commitment form
existing.selection_notes: Evaluated based on research proposal quality, significance of contributions, and suitability of proposed research environment. Some awards reserved for Black postdoctoral researchers who self-identify.
existing.best_fit: Top-tier postdoctoral researchers seeking advanced research training in Canada.
existing.notes: Replaces the Banting Postdoctoral Fellowships and former CIHR/NSERC/SSHRC postdoctoral fellowships. Maximum three lifetime applications permitted.
existing.deadline_display: Application deadline: September 10, 2026 (8:00 p.m. eastern) for the September 2026 Competition. This deadline has passed as at 2026-10-04; the next annual competition date was not published on the page read.
existing.program_type: Federal research training award (Canada Postdoctoral Research Award program)

scholarships.title: Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development - Phase 2 (SEED-2)

existing.description: The Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development - Phase 2 (SEED-2) program is offered by Global Affairs Canada as a key initiative under Canada's Indo-Pacific Strategy, funded under that strategy. It expands the Canada-ASEAN Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development (SEED) programme to students from ASEAN Member States, Pacific Island Countries and Mongolia, who conduct short-term study or research at Canadian post-secondary institutions in areas contributing to the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Canadian institutions must apply on behalf of eligible candidates, must be Designated Learning Institutions, and must waive tuition fees for recipients. Four award components are offered, from $10,200 to $15,900, with durations of four to eight months.
eligibility: Citizen of an ASEAN Member State, a Pacific Island Country or Mongolia (the 30 eligible countries are listed on the official page)
Enrolled full-time at a post-secondary institution in an eligible country
Paying tuition fees to that institution at the time of application and for the full duration of the exchange
Not hold or have pending an application for Canadian citizenship or permanent residency
Not already participating in a scholarship program funded by the Government of Canada
Not already enrolled in a degree, diploma or certificate program at a Canadian post-secondary institution
Not have previously received a scholarship under the first phase of the program (Canada-ASEAN SEED)
Canadian host institution must be a Designated Learning Institution, must waive tuition fees for scholarship recipients, and must centralize applications through its international office
existing.eligibility_summary: Candidates must be citizens of an ASEAN Member State (Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste or Vietnam), a Pacific Island Country (Cook Islands, Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Nauru, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu or Vanuatu), or Mongolia; be enrolled full-time at a post-secondary institution in an eligible country; and be paying tuition fees to that institution at the time of application and for the full duration of the exchange. Hosting Canadian institutions must be a Designated Learning Institution, must waive tuition fees for scholarship recipients, and must centralize applications through their international office.
benefits: Airfare to Canada via the most direct and economical route
Living expenses including accommodation, utilities and food
Ground transportation including a public transportation pass
Books and supplies for the study or research (computers and other equipment excluded)
Canadian institutions additionally receive $500 per scholarship recipient for administrative costs and, in some cases, reimbursement of additional employer compliance fees paid to IRCC
coverage: Eligible expenses: visa or study/work permit fees; airfare via the most direct and economical route; health insurance; living expenses such as accommodation, utilities and food; ground transportation including a public transportation pass; books and supplies required for the study or research, excluding computers and other equipment
Tuition must be waived by the Canadian host institution
requirements: Be nominated by a Canadian host institution, which must apply on the candidate's behalf through My EduCanada

Provide a one-page letter of intent that identifies the Sustainable Development Goal the proposed study or research aligns with - 'letters that do not identify an SDG will be deemed incomplete and not eligible'
Provide country-specific poverty-impact explanations where required
Provide a letter of proof of full-time enrolment on official letterhead dated within the last six months
Provide a one-page letter of support from the home institution on official letterhead dated within the last six months
Graduate applicants must provide a one-page letter of invitation from the Canadian supervisor
Upload all supporting documents in the accepted formats, each smaller than 5 MB
documents: Letter of support from home university
existing.english_requirement: Not stated as an applicant requirement. The official page states that 'Documents in a language other than English or French must be accompanied by a translation', so English or French is the working language of the application.
application_method: The Canadian institution assigns a program coordinator, creates a My EduCanada account via Global Affairs Canada Single Sign-On (a GCKey account is recommended), selects the SEED-2 programme and clicks Apply
The institution enters candidate data, validates and saves, uploads all required supporting documents, accepts the Declaration and permission statement and submits
The institution separately emails a ranking of applications based on its strategic priorities to seed-bpeed@international.gc.ca, indicating each candidate's MyEduCanada application number
Institutions are encouraged to set an earlier internal deadline with candidates and their home institutions
existing.selection_notes: Global Affairs Canada reviews applications based on alignment with Sustainable Development Goals, research merit, and institutional partnerships.
existing.best_fit: Students from eligible Indo-Pacific countries seeking short-term academic or research exchanges at Canadian universities.
existing.notes: Non-deferrable and non-renewable. Students must return to home institution after exchange. Tuition is waived by the Canadian host institution.
existing.duration: Four to eight months: college/undergraduate 4 months or 8 months (two academic terms); graduate 4 months or 5 to 6 months. Scholarships cannot be deferred and are not renewable.
existing.application_period: Applications open January 2026; institutional deadline March 24, 2026
existing.deadline_display: Canadian institutions must apply on behalf of eligible candidates before the deadline of 11:59 p.m. EDT, March 24, 2026. The page states 'Application period for 2026-27 is closed.' Institutions are encouraged to set an earlier internal deadline with candidates and their home institutions.
